About

THE DESIGNER
BEHIND THE WORK

I am a Product Designer and Experience Research Strategist who has spent 18+ years making complex enterprise systems feel intuitive, human, and worth using.

My work spans enterprise intranet platforms, AI-assisted interfaces, conversational UX, content authoring systems, and search - across financial services, B2B, public sector, and consumer products.

What makes me different is a grounding in Behavioural Psychology (Pursuing my MA at MIT) - I don't just observe what users do, I understand why they feel stuck, uncertain, or capable. That shapes every design decision, from taxonomy to tone of voice.

"I design for the person who has no choice but to use the tool - and that responsibility shapes every decision."

I've led cross-functional teams across engineering, product, and content. I'm comfortable with ambiguity, energised by complex systems, and deeply committed to accessibility and inclusive design.

LET'S WORK TOGETHER

Artwork Dashboard - Status filtering & version tracking
Artwork Editor - Smart file lock & approval workflow
The Problem

Nobody knew who had the latest file. Conflicting edits overwrote each other with no version history, no lock mechanism, and approval chains lost in email - causing costly print errors across pharmaceutical and FMCG labelling.

Research
  • 38 users interviewed - designers, approvers, ops managers across 4 countries
  • Shadowed 8 users during live sessions - observed real version confusion
  • Mapped 12 end-to-end artwork tasks to find where workflow broke down most
  • Benchmarked 6 DAM tools for version control UX patterns and approval flows
Design Decisions
  • Smart File Locking - auto-locks on edit; others see "locked by [name]"
  • Version Timeline - full edit history with one-click rollback
  • Approval Chain - Draft -> Review -> Approved -> Published with audit trail
  • ML Language Check - flags region-specific compliance issues inline

Key Finding

The Problem

Enterprise authors were expected to build high-quality digital experiences without enough support for information architecture, accessibility, taxonomy, governance, or localisation. That meant pages were often structurally inconsistent, difficult to search, and expensive to fix after publishing.

The bigger opportunity was not just content generation. It was helping authors make better experience decisions earlier: what to show, how to structure it, how to adapt it by region, and how to stay compliant without depending on specialist review for every draft.

What I Designed
  • Prompt-to-Structure Workflow - turns author intent into a draft page model, not just text blocks.
  • In-Context Guidance - accessibility, metadata, and governance prompts appear alongside authoring decisions.
  • Regional Adaptation Layer - shared experience patterns can flex for India, UK, and US policy needs.
  • Human Review Controls - AI recommendations stay editable so authors keep ownership and confidence.
Design Decisions
  • Kept the workspace modular so authors could inspect structure, content quality, and governance separately without feeling overwhelmed.
  • Used recommendation chips and plain-language diagnostics instead of opaque AI scores, making the system easier to trust.
  • Designed for teams, not solo authors, so outputs could be reviewed, shared, and scaled across multiple business units.

PropSys 360 — Asset Management Platform
Neo Technology / UK Social Housing — Lead Product UX Designer · 20 Weeks
Enterprise Dashboard UK Social Housing Multi-Role UX KPI & ROI Metrics
Product Screens
Director of Assets dashboard — portfolio-wide KPIs, DHS score, overdue items, and cost analysis in a single view.
Void Manager dashboard — re-let velocity, rent loss exposure, first-time clearance rate, and post-move-in CSAT.
The Challenge

A UK social housing association managing 50,000+ units across 20,000 sites had no unified digital platform. Four distinct operational roles — Director of Assets, Void Manager, Compliance Officer, and Repairs Manager — each relied on separate spreadsheets, email chains, and legacy tools to track KPIs, compliance obligations, and repair workflows. Data was siloed, decisions were delayed, and costly compliance failures were going undetected until they became regulatory incidents.

The brief was ambitious: design a single platform that could surface the right information to the right person at the right time — without forcing every role into the same one-size-fits-all view.

My Role & Approach

I led discovery, information architecture, UX design, and prototyping across all four role tracks in parallel. I facilitated workshops with Housing Directors, Void Managers, Compliance teams, and Field Repair staff to map their distinct mental models, decision triggers, and data needs. The key insight: each role defined "urgent" differently. A compliance officer responds to certificate expiry. A void manager responds to re-let timeline slippage. A repairs manager responds to SLA breach risk. One dashboard could not serve all four.

The 4 Role Dashboards
DIRECTOR OF ASSETS
Portfolio-wide KPIs. Decent Homes Standard score (target 95%). Overdue compliance certs. Cost analysis vs estimated. Stock condition surveys. Program builder for capital works.
VOID MANAGER
Void pipeline by stage (Inspection → Repair → Ready to Let). Average re-let time vs 30-day target. Cost per void vs £1200 standard. Rent loss exposure. First-time lettable clearance rate. Post-move-in CSAT.
COMPLIANCE OFFICER
Gas safety, EPC, fire risk, and electrical certificates by status. Overdue count with escalation flags. Upcoming expiry calendar. Regulatory risk score per property block.
REPAIRS MANAGER
Active cases by type: Disrepair, Damp & Mould, Major. Work order queue with SLA status. Contractor assignment. Component replacement tracking. Repairs cost vs budget.

Key Design Decisions
  • Role-Adaptive Entry Points — Login detects user role and routes to their specialised dashboard. No configuration required. Each view surfaces only the alerts, metrics, and actions relevant to that role.
  • Smart Alert System — System-flagged data issues and inspection triggers appear as contextual banners with inline "Review" CTAs, not buried in notification panels.
  • Progress vs Target Design — Every KPI shows current value alongside target threshold (e.g. 30-day re-let target, £1200 cost-per-void standard) so users can self-assess performance without digging into reports.
  • Audit Trail & Activity Feed — A time-stamped activity sidebar gives all roles visibility of recent actions (surveys completed, certificates issued, void status changes) to replace manual status emails.
  • Responsive Hierarchy — Sites → Block → Core → Units drill-down model with 20K sites and 50K units required a spatial hierarchy navigation pattern, not flat search.
